summary: The North American trek kicked off in Denver on June 26.
body: Chris Brown and Usher joined forces this year for a once-in-a-generation tour. title: Mariah Carey Wins Dismissal of Brother’s Defamation Lawsuit Over Bestselling Memoir
summary: The singer's lawyer says she's "gratified" by the court ruling. Her brother, Morgan Carey, plans to appeal.
body: Mariah Carey has defeated a long-running lawsuit that alleged she defamed her brother in her bestselling 2020 memoir The Meaning of Mariah Carey . In a Monday (Oct. 19) court order, obtained and first reported by Billboard , a judge ruled that Morgan Carey has not met the requirements to sue his superstar sister over passages of her book that suggested he had sold cocaine and done prison time. New York law requires a defamation lawsuit against a public figure to plead “actual malice” — that is, demonstrate that they lied on purpose. title: Quevedo & Kidd Voodoo Talk New Urban Movement: ‘One of the Things That Makes Us Unique Is Where We Come From’
summary: From the Canary Islands and Chile, the artists discussed identity and the global expansion of their respective scenes during Billboard Latin Music Week.
body: Urban music no longer moves in just one direction. It travels across islands, continents and platforms, absorbing local sounds and transforming them into global anthems. That was one of the central ideas of The New Urban Movement, a conversation featuring Quevedo and Kidd Voodoo on Monday (Oct. 19) during Billboard Latin Music Week 2026 . Moderated by Billboard associate editor Jessica Roiz, the panel took place at the Faena Theater in Miami Beach. Both artists discussed how their places of origin have shaped their music. “One of the things that makes us unique is where we come from,” Quevedo said. For him, growing up in the Canary Islands — a territory historically connected to Latin America — was essential to developing the identity of Buenas Noches (2024) and El Baifo (2026), an urban album that also incorporates merengue, salsa and other Latin rhythms. “Talking about our own experiences makes us artists more unique,” he added. He also reflected on the impact of his 2022 collaboration with Bizarrap, which topped Billboard ’s Latin Airplay, Billboard Global 200 and Billboard Global Excl. title: Google is giving you more creative control over Gemini Notebook’s video overviews and slides
summary: Google will soon roll out "co-creation" capabilities for two of Gemini Notebook's most popular features.
body: Credit: Karandeep Singh / Android Authority TL;DR Gemini Notebook is giving users more creative control over Slide Decks and Video Overviews through a feature called “Co-creation.” The platform will now walk the user through the creation flow, allowing them to steer the format and visual style before the final output. Co-creation capabilities will roll out to all users over the upcoming week. Gemini Notebook is a helpful tool for digesting large amounts of information. One way this is done is by breaking down your material into structured formats such as Audio Overviews and Study Aids, like flashcards. After a new update, you’ll soon have more creative control over the output from two of these formats. In a blog post , Google announced that it will add “co-creation” capabilities to Video Overviews and Slide Decks. Normally, Gemini Notebook will take a prompt and jump right to the final product. However, with co-creation, Notebook will walk you through the creation flow before outputting a result.

title: TP-Link signs deal to produce Wi-Fi 8 routers in US amid FCC ban
summary: Starting early next year, Wi-Fi 8 routers will be assembled by Key Tronic in Mississippi.
body: TL;DR TP-Link signs letter of intent with Key Tronic to build Wi-Fi 8 routers in Mississippi. Manufacture will begin early next year. TP-Link continues to pursue exemption from FCC ban while it faces lawsuits. The impact of the ban on foreign-made routers that the FCC implemented in March is still causing reverberations. While some router manufacturers have received exemptions , one of the largest, TP-Link is not among them. Now the company looks like it might have found a way to keep selling routers in the United States. TP-Link has announced a partnership with tech manufacturer Key Tronic Corporation to assemble its products in the United States, beginning with production of its Wi-Fi 8 routers in Mississippi (via PCMag ). Production will begin “as early as next year.”

title: This magnetic accessory brings true flash back to phones
summary: The $85 accessory is iPhone-only for now, but Godox says Android support is coming.
body: TL;DR The $85 Godox A2 brings real xenon flash to smartphones. It’s iPhone-only for now, but the company says Android support is “under development.” Android devices led the way with built-in xenon flash, but abandoned the idea over a decade ago. For as outdated as it is, the image of a flashbulb going off as a button is pressed is one of the most universally recognizable signs of a photo being taken. And yet, our phones, which capture the majority of our photos , use LED flashes that don’t produce the same blinding intensity of light (or image quality) that are the result of “real” flash. But they can with the just introduced Godox A2, an accessory that uses a xenon flash tube and magnetically attaches to phones. The Godox A2 sells for $85, but don’t expect to order one for your Android device in the near future (via The Verge ). It’s iPhone-only for now, though on the product page, the company says that Android support is “under development.” Because the Godox A2 relies on a magnetic connection, like Apple’s MagSafe, it won’t work with every Android device. Right now that means Android phones with native support, like Pixel models since the 10 series or the Motorola Edge 70 Max …

title: Google Play Store bug is causing Collections confusion
summary: Is your Play Store Collections shortcut icon missing? You’re not alone.
body: Credit: C. Scott Brown / Android Authority TL;DR A visual glitch is affecting the Play Store’s Collections shortcut on the stock Pixel Launcher. Users are reporting that the icon next to the Collections shortcut is completely blank. Google’s Pixel product support team recommends checking for updates, clearing the Pixel Launcher cache, or rebooting into safe mode to see if a third-party app is the issue. It has been about two years since Google introduced the Play Store feature known as “ Collections .” This feature organizes your apps by topic and highlights content recommended by your apps. It’s meant to help you discover new content or resume content already in progress right from your home screen. If you tried to set up the widget recently, you may have noticed that something is a little off. Accessing Collections is as easy as long-pressing on the Play Store app. It appears as the last option in the pop-up menu. Normally, the Collections option is accompanied by an icon in a circular enclosure. However, a bug appears to be causing a visual glitch.

title: Spotify is cracking down on Family plan sharing, but you can still bypass the checks
summary: The streaming platform is using dynamic QR codes to enforce household rules this time.
body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR Spotify is cracking down on Family plan sharing by requiring members to complete dynamic QR code address scans in person. Unverified users have seven days to complete the scan or face demotion to the Free tier and a 12-month ban on joining shared Family or Duo plans. Screenshots aren’t feasible with these dynamic QR codes, so subscribers are sidestepping the check by screen-sharing across multiple devices. Spotify is stepping up enforcement of its household location rules, leaving several Premium Family plan subscribers suddenly booted off their shared plans. The streaming giant is cracking down on family plan sharing to ensure that all members reside at the same location as the plan manager. A growing number of Reddit users are reporting that Spotify Family plan account holders are receiving sudden address re-verification prompts, particularly if they are not at the same location as other users on the Family plan. This re-verification is seemingly being done in person, with constantly refreshing QR code scans between the plan manager’s device and the member’s phone to confirm they live in the same household.

body: I got my hands on the Google Pixel 11 Pro XL when it launched globally in August, and I’ve spent quite a bit of time with it since. It’s not my daily driver, but I’ve used it enough to know what I love about it and, more importantly, where I wish Google had done things differently. If there’s one thing I’ve come to appreciate about Pixel phones over the years, it’s how Google gets so many of the little things right. From the design and software to how everything feels in everyday use, using a Pixel has a certain charm that’s hard to ignore. Of course, that doesn’t mean everything is perfect. Smartwatches deliver a constant stream of information to our wrists, but one thing they’re not always clued in about is their own demise. title: Hate the idea of paying for YouTube Premium? Imagine paying $240 a year for regular YouTube
summary: YouTube's next big fee might not even come from Google.
body: TL;DR The UK government is considering expanding its annual £180 (~$240) TV license fee to cover on-demand streaming services like YouTube, Netflix, and Disney Plus. If implemented, the change could require households to pay a license fee even to watch regular YouTube videos, without getting any Premium benefits. The proposal aims to address declining BBC funding but hasn’t been finalized. Does nothing sound worse than the idea of paying for YouTube Premium ? Well, imagine having to pay the government just for getting access to regular YouTube with none of the Premium perks attached. Sounds ridiculous, right? Unfortunately, that’s a possibility under consideration in the UK. To truly understand the development, you first need to understand the concept of a TV license fee in the UK. By law, you must have a TV license (£180 per year/~$240) if you plan on watching or recording programs as they’re being shown on live TV. You also need a license if you plan on watching or streaming programs live on online TV services, including the likes of YouTube, Netflix, and even Amazon Prime Video. You do not need a license if you’re only watching on-demand content on these platforms, like our lat…

The fix seems to rely on a mix of app updates and server-side flags, so a full rollout across all devices may still take weeks. If you have been driving blind to your phone’s cellular connectivity, relief is finally rolling out. Google appears to be widening the rollout of a fix that restores the missing network signal icon in Android Auto , addressing a frustrating bug that left drivers guessing whether their phone actually had reception.
